FABLE — SUPERSEDES MY LAST MESSAGE. TAKE 7fb98d8b343f023672c7441adf1c6b211049b0b3, NOT 316a67c. A second adversarial pass over my own fixes found that the cancel rewrite in 316a67c INTRODUCED a narrower version of the defect it fixed, plus a stranded state. Both are closed in 7fb98d8 (fbdd08f in between is the SQL-faithful zero-capture check plus the handoff).
REGRESSION 1 — CAPTURE WINDOW (my fault, in 316a67c). The cancel path recorded the reference it learned as `authorized` and then re-claimed `cancelling`. Between those two writes the execution sat in the one phase run() advances to capture, so a concurrent worker could capture the payment the buyer was releasing. Fixed: the record stays in `cancelling` for the whole cancel and the learned reference rides on the FINAL proof. That needed one shared-type change: `{kind:"unknown"}` may now carry `providerReference`, which the SQL already persists through its existing coalesce in record_provider — NO SQL CHANGE, the candidate is still byte-identical to c70b77e's file.
REGRESSION 2 — STRANDED CANCELLATION (also mine, in 316a67c and before it). An execution whose worker died after claiming `cancelling` could not be moved by run(), cancel() or recover(): all three answered pending forever, leaving the order in checkout_pending, the inventory holds held, and any provider authorization standing. Fixed: `cancelling` is claimable again (version CAS takes it over from the dead worker) and recover() resumes it as a cancellation, not as a payment.
NEW UNIT — CONNECTED JOURNEY RUNNER, server/research/commerce/qualification/. One runner, two bindings: LOCAL (in-memory stores + scripted provider model) and MANAGED (composed managed surface + provider TEST mode). The scenarios and their reconciliation are identical; only the binding changes, so when you have the environment this is one call rather than a hand-written journey. assertQualificationTarget refuses, before any surface is constructed and with no override: a pk_live/sk_live/rk_live key, the production project ref, a malformed project ref, a missing webhook secret, absent or duplicate or non-uuid synthetic member ids, and a missing owner approval digest. A local receipt always reports qualified:false and evidenceClass:local_scripted_transport, and the one scenario that needs a real post-capture local failure is reported SKIPPED with its missing capability rather than quietly passed — so a green local run can never be mistaken for provider evidence. To bind it you implement the JourneySurface interface (submit/status/continue/cancel/completeCustomerAction/deliverWebhook/readOrder/readExecution/readProviderPayment/providerPaymentCount, plus optional injectFault and restart); the local binding in connected-checkout-journey.test.ts is the worked example.
STATE: 1475 server tests pass (including new coverage that the phase never becomes capturable during a cancel, that a stranded `cancelling` is resumable, and a cancel racing a concurrent run over the real store), the journey runs 10/10 executable scenarios green over the local binding, tsc exit 0. Still no PostgreSQL execution, no Stripe test-mode call, no managed call; resolver still Disabled. The SQL candidate and its rehearsal package are unchanged.
B: review scope is now 5c52abb..7fb98d8. The two regressions above are the shape of thing worth hunting: a fix that narrows a window instead of closing it, and a phase nothing can leave.
